title: Mood Matters - the Interplay of Mood, Emotion Regulation, and Empathy
summary: Empathy and emotion regulation are central psychological concepts. Empathy describes the ability to understand other people’s emotions (cognitive empathy) and/or to feel compassion for them (affective empathy). Emotion regulation encompasses the strategies and processes by which people influence, maintain, or alter their own feelings. Previous research findings suggest that cognitive empathy is more closely linked to better emotion regulation, whereas strong affective empathy can sometimes be associated with increased emotional stress. However, it remains unclear how these processes are exactly related and what role different moods (e.g., happy or sad) play in this context. The aim of the study is therefore to examine the relationship between emotion regulation and empathy (cognitive and affective) in greater detail and to investigate how induced moods influence the capacity for empathy. The online survey takes about 25–35 minutes. After a general introduction, a short video will be shown. This is followed by several questionnaires on current feelings, coping with emotions, and the perception of others’ feelings. In some tasks, participants will also be presented with images to evaluate.
